evidence: A calculation on committed products: a mean-geometry ephemeris of the turned Moon in Cassini state 2; the light calendar's clear-sky evaluator on the solved 1.2-atm column; photons per lux from the solved standard solution's channels; the run's cloud cover in a two-state sky with an Earth overcast transmission; LOLA terrain with the atlas's seas and the routed lakes. Not observations, not a climate run, not validated against measured light on any Moon; the twilight and clear sky are the solved molecular column's (no aerosol, no refraction in the scattering).
reading_rule: Latitudes are the turned Moon's (north positive). The eclipse-year phase u is 0 at the Sun's northward crossing of the lunar equator, 90 at the north's midsummer and 270 at the south's; season tables hold u = 0, 30, ..., 330 at the lunar day's local noon. A lunar day is 708.7 hours, midnight to midnight. dli values are mol/m2 per 24 hours averaged over the lunar day (the lunar day's photons / 29.53); dli24 the lowest and highest 24-hour window inside it. Hours are per lunar day. "cloud" is the expected value in the two-state sky with the run's cover; "overcast" the whole day under cloud. Light is on level, open ground unless a terrain section says otherwise; the run's precession phase (south summer at perihelion) unless a key names another. Annual values weight each season by the time the Sun spends there. Pairs in tilt_and_precession are [tilt 1.613, tilt 2.5] or [run phase, north summer at perihelion]. Terrain quantiles are [10th, 50th, 90th] percentiles by area.
assumptions: Mean geometry: uniform rotation, the Sun's hour angle at the mean synodic rate, the Sun's declination from the eclipse-year phase, the Earth's orbit with the run's year and eccentricity; a mean Earth distance and sinusoidal libration in longitude; good to a few tenths of a degree, not an ephemeris for dates

Clear-sky light is the calendar evaluator's: one horizontally uniform 1.2-atm molecular column, Lambertian ground of albedo 0.1, no aerosol; refraction is computed apart and enters only the hours the Sun is up

Clouds: the run's cover by latitude and hour angle in a two-state sky; overcast passes 0.25 of the clear sky's light at every Sun height and in twilight (an Earth relation); the run's own surface sunlight cannot serve as a cloud transmission in the polar rows (see clouds.run_sunlight_diagnostic)

Terrain: horizons on a 1.9 km grid to 265 km, nearest-neighbour samples; light on horizontal ground, no light reflected from the terrain itself, no sloped surfaces; seas at the atlas's level and the routed lakes as flat water
Earthlight carries sunlight's photons per lux for the sky at the Earth's height; at most a few lux at the poles
